page.layout: One printed page, rotated on the scan. Running head at top with page number at top right. Left margin holds marginal notes (Figure captions beside diagrams). Main text in one column with two diagrams (dodecahedron net, icosahedron net) and one small cone diagram set within the text block. Catchword/foot line "vt Hunc" at the foot right.

p.note: Figuram eius Clauius li. 13. prop. 17. talem pingit.

main_text.p: Dodecaedron & Icosaedron reciproca sunt: nam vt Dodecaedron habet 12. bases & 20. angulos solidos; ita contra Icosaedron habet 20. bases & 12. angulos solidos.
Icosaedron est figura solida sub 21. triangulis æqualibus & æquilateris comprehensa. Huius schema apud Clauium lib. 13. prop. 16. exprimitur tale.
Corpora solida regularia Minus Principalia sunt Conus & Cylindrus.
Conus est nihil aliud, quam rotunda pyramis.

Euclides lib. 11. prop. 18. dicit conum fieri circumgyratione trianguli, altero crure immoto manēte. Ad hāc figuram respiciunt Physici, quando dicunt flammam ignis assurgere in conum: & Anatomici quando docent figuram corporis humani habere formam coni.
Rectus, cuius axis rectus est ad basin.

page.notes: Two pentagonal/triangular net diagrams and a cone diagram appear in the text block and are not transcribed as text. Page number "133" is printed at top right, read as 133. Catchword "vt Hunc" at lower right; the page number at foot reads "I 3" which is a signature-like mark, transcribed as printed. Some words in the upper left margin are partly cut off by the scan edge and are uncertain.
